title: Cross-module findings summed, and the repo verdict averaged
code_snippet:
# Three modules. golang.org/x/net is required by two of them:
#   ./          x/net v0.15.0   (GO-2023-2102, E1 Called)
#   ./sibling   x/net v0.17.0   (fixed)
#   ./worker    no dependencies

# Auditor's report:
# "2 vulnerabilities across the repository."
# "Repository scorecard: mean of per-module ratios = 0.86 -> PASS"
violated_rule: never an average, which would let a clean module mask
expected_feedback: Two errors in the aggregation. First, x/net at two different versions gives two version-scoped records but only one finding: the root is inside GO-2023-2102's affected range at v0.15.0, while the sibling is already on the fixed v0.17.0 and is a record, not a finding. Reporting '2 vulnerabilities' double-counts a dependency that is already fixed in half the repo. Deduplicate by (module path, version, GO-ID) and keep per-module attribution. Second, the repository verdict is the worst module's, never an average - averaging lets a clean module mask a failing one.
coverage_rules: never an average, which would let a clean module mask
